rows.text: Amphoreus, The Eternal Land...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Huh? Has it been that long?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Alright, then. For now, I'll let Miss Black Swan know that we're considering The Eternal Land as a destination.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Of course you can. For now, I'll let Miss Black Swan know that we're considering The Eternal Land as a possible destination, but we're also keeping our options open.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: There is no record of this world in the data bank... Not even a mention of its name.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There's no need to be nervous. I understand that it may be difficult for us today to wrap our heads around the idea that there's a world Akivili didn't venture into, but a journey like that was only routine to the Express Crew back then. After all, to trailblaze is to explore the universe's boundaries.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We should consider Pom-Pom's opinion, too. They don't know we're considering Amphoreus as a destination.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Sure, I'll take care of it. That said, Pom-Pom usually stays out of discussions about destinations. The final decision will likely still be on us to make.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In that case, we'd best take the time to think this over.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah! Plus, even if we pass Amphoreus over, we've still got a fuel problem to solve.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seeing as how this is going to be an unusual adventure, it'd be good for us to take some time out to make preparations for the journey. Meanwhile, I'll see if I can find out more about Amphoreus from our allies before we depart.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In other words, we won't be leaving Penacony anytime soon.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Or we could also revisit our previous stops to make sure that the astral charts and navigation routes are all functioning fine? I wonder if the hole in the Taikiyan Stadium has been repaired.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Express has been on the go almost the whole time since we left the space station. We've barely had any time to catch our breath. Let's take this as an opportunity to wrap up our vacation instead, and make the most out of this break.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: At this moment, people still haven't expected this vacation to be so fulfilling. They will witness the grand Xianzhou wardance and, during this moment of leisure, also complete arts promise made by a genius...
And those they will meet again... include not only friends, but also foes.
Creating chaos is also a means to maintaining social stability, if you ask me.
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: If you have the time for mindless gossip, you're probably better off spending it on getting actual work done.
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: They say this is all part of "ongoing investigations," but is there even any point to doing this? The threat's long been neutralized. They're just putting on a show.
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: I mean, look at us, and this sudden surge in inter-Family cooperative efforts. It's nothing but a pretense for those outsiders, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: Sounds like you've got insider intel. Now I'm curious...
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Are the stories going around true? Was the furor that broke out a while ago really a result of trouble within the Oak Family?
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Those are some difficult questions... Didn't I just say that creating chaos is also a means to maintaining social stability?
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: Who knows who's been fanning the flames, but there are a dozen rumors going around out there, each one more outlandish than the last.
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: You insert Pleasant-Looking Trash into the bin as a sign of consideration, and in the blink of an eye, more Pleasant-Looking Trashes emerge — what an inappropriate application of the Horn of Plenty concept.
You insert more Pleasant-Looking Trash. The trashcan is overjoyed and silently pays its respects to you. Before you leave, you suddenly feel a sense of dignity.

Oh, I've heard those. Conspiracy theories about how the IPC had orchestrated everything and... What was it again? That the chaos was only quelled because of an accident? Ugh, it makes no sense. So, what's the lowdown?
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: The truth has probably been long buried under all the hearsay. All I can say for sure is that someone's taken the rap for it.
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: You mean... the former Oak Family head?
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Bingo! Most of the blame was pinned on him when the Charmony Festival was abruptly canceled. Since then, not a single soul's seen him.
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: Heck, forget his whereabouts — nobody even knows if he's still alive! Talk about scary. For all we know, we might have watched something go down in history — like what happened to the Blackplum Family back then — without even realizing it.
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: You attempt to insert some things, but no reaction is observed — This little trashcan has quite the personality, successfully grabbing your attention.
I've heard another theory about that family head, though...
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: I beg your pardon, sirs. Dreamweavers are carrying out inspections on the routes around here, and all affected facilities have been closed off. Kindly take a detour in the meantime.
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: What happened? Is this because of the Stellaron? Geez, are we Penaconians never gonna dream in peace again?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: There is no cause for alarm, sir. The Stellaron has already been sealed. This is just a routine inspection. A move to heighten security, if you will.
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: Please rest assured that The Family will do everything in our power to protect the sweet dreams of every guest.
rows.speaker: Nightingale Family Member

rows.text: I see. We'll leave the two of you to your work, then.
rows.speaker: Weary Passerby

rows.text: ...Hmm?
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Excuse me, sir...
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Have we met before?
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: Do you recall when or where we might've met?
rows.speaker: Weary Passerby

rows.text: My bad, I must be mistaken. Sorry about that. Sweet dreams to both of you, sirs.
rows.speaker: Bloodhound Family Member

rows.text: You sure have a knack for stirring up trouble. Of all the routes available, you had to take the one that Bloodhound's keeping watch over.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: We shouldn't run into any problems with you around. Even if they see through the Harmony's power of disguise, there'll be a way for us to escape.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Spare a thought for me, will you? Just being in your company is plenty enough to get me into trouble, Mr. Prime Fugitive of Penacony.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: And that is exactly why I need you with me. You're the only one I can rely on in Penacony now.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hmph, the only one you can rely on, huh.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: What about her?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: At least she was spared from the consequences of my actions.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What a shame, huh?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Why do you say that?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Just thought that being mean might be more effective than consoling you.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I've seen plenty like you. Eager for everyone to take you to task after a setback because that's the only way you'll feel better. As though the more they condemn you, the more likely you can rectify your mistake.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: That said, if I'd really wanted to hit you where it hurts, I'd use a different approach... Like a show of sympathy, for example.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: You're right. I won't deny that.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: She should still be in Penacony. Aren't you going to look for her?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: That won't be necessary. I'm sure you already know why, considering your vested interest in reading my thoughts.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...I can't bring myself to see her when I'm a fugitive.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I see two Bloodhounds... They appear to be on official business, unlike the pair from earlier.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What's happening at Aideen Park?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hey! Heeeey! In case you didn't notice, I can't see anything!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: My apologies. I forgot that you're not very tall.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Remind me... Why do I have to make this trip with you again?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: We've been through this. You're the only one I can turn to now.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Besides, we once lived a cat-and-dog existence. Embroiling you in my affairs won't weigh on my conscience.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You certainly don't have much of one if you can bring yourself to say something like that.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Yet you will repay this favor all the same. After all, you're only alive today because of me. You owe me that much.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Holy moly! Can you get any more conceited?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: When you were abandoned in the wild and near your end, I showed you a way to survive and helped you escape the jaws of death.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: When you were at your wits' end and felt lost about your future, I did everything within my power to help you safeguard your position in The Family.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Okay, okay. I get it already. You have a way with words, I'll give you that. Still, it's one thing to repay a favor, but quite another to knowingly put myself in harm's way.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I don't understand. Why are you hell-bent on going back to Penacony? Is this an IPC mission?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Did they make you a deal? "You can have your freedom back, but in return, you must turn against all whom you once called family" or something like that?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Regrettably, Lady Bonajade didn't drop so much as a hint about it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Go now. You are free — O chosen one, who dared to exceed his bounds. Sever your wings, descend to the mortal realm, and walk their lands. See what this world is truly like.
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: I will not accept your charity.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: As I mentioned earlier: It's a trade, and you don't have to give me an answer right now. Rewards are not reaped in a day, and if there's one thing I'm best at, it's waiting. The sweet dream still continues, and the night is still long — you have plenty of time to contemplate your answer.
rows.speaker: Jade

rows.text: She only left me with a most intriguing message before setting me free. As for whether I can afford the price of my freedom...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'll only know when I find out what it is.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But nothing good ever comes out of being in the IPC's debt.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I'll cross that bridge when I get to it. For now, there's still some time before that payment is due, so why not exercise the right to freedom that I've just regained?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: By walking straight into a trap?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Or by making amends for past deeds.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: When it's time to go, this will be farewell for good. So, before I leave Penacony, I'd like to take some time to look back on all the events that have taken place.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Can't you just look back on it from a distance?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: There's something else I want to do, too. The Embryo of Philosophy may have fallen, but the Order in Penacony wasn't built in a day. This sweet dream is likely to still contain residual traces of the Oak Family's influence.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Get off your high horse. The other four Families are more than capable of working things out on their own.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I might have gone astray, but others shouldn't have to clean up after my mistakes.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Then you should also know that the IPC isn't going to help you a second time. If you fall into The Family's hands again, you're done for.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: You know how it is — old habits die hard.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The tie should be on the center line, the shirt must not protrude from the vest, trouser creases should be perfectly straight, and always aligned with the tips of your shoes.... We should always ensure that everything is in order before walking out the door.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The same applies when bidding my home farewell, too.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But what has Aideen Park got to do with you? Don't tell me that the founder's one of your disguises?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I'm not that old.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Oh, come on. Take a joke, will you?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: You shouldn't have said that just now. It'll only make us look suspicious.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Said what?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: "Mr. Workday."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hmph, I was just telling the truth. I've always found this name to be more suitable for you.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Like a drunkard commonly seen by the sidewalk, he vomited a sliver of rainbow—
So, why are we here? You managed this park before?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: You could say that. I was still a child back then. To become the Bronze Melodia of the Oak Family, I'd gone under Mr. Gopher Wood's tutelage.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: We were taking a walk in the park like any other day when he suddenly hit on the idea to have me manage the park. Within the domain he demarcated, my every word would hold the force of law.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: In hindsight, that was probably the first time that I enforced Order.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You rose through the ranks soon after. I take it that you must have done a pretty good job?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Quite the contrary — I made a terrible mess of things. Fortunately, the tourists thought of it as nothing more than a spell of merrymaking.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Was that his way of training you?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Perhaps he was just using an approach with lighter consequences to show me what he'd learned in life: That there is never an ideal paradigm when it comes to rules. If the enforcer is incapable of introspection, then even regulations once laid down with the noblest of intentions will eventually become defiled.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This place is no exception. The distorted Afterechoes of the Order... will only add to the chaos.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Let's see what we have on these notes...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Next on the list is the stage. Let's go and check it out.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: "Only cast and crew members are allowed on the stage." Hm, a surprisingly reasonable rule.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: And an easy one to test. Neither of us is part of the cast or a crew member. Let's try it out.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Huh?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Let's try that again.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What's going on?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: "Guide those who have lost their way back onto the right path." Looks like this is an example of the "corrective measures" that the Bloodhound mentioned. It's exactly what I would've done back then.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You've been iron-fisted since you were little, haven't you?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: ...Wait a sec. If this is how violations are corrected, then everything that I ate just now...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I tried to warn you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Ugh...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: How do you feel?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Now, I'm feeling murderous...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: In any case, say what you will, but I can't sit by and do nothing. Not when I'm the cause of all this trouble in Aideen Park. There's no need to involve the Dreamweavers. I'll fix these distortions once and for all.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What's the plan?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Nothing complicated. All distortions have their roots. We'll be able to trace them to the source once they manifest. Breaking a few rules will do. We just need to make sure that the corrective measures that will be implemented aren't too much for us to handle.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: When a distorted Afterecho manifests to correct us, I'll be able to pinpoint its whereabouts.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Then I'll use the power of tuning to heal the Dreamscape.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Be kind to birds."
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Looks like some rules weren't distorted. That's a word-for-word account of what I said back then.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Did you make this rule because your sister is named Robin?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: No, it was for Mr. Gopher Wood. He used to stop by the park to people-watch and appreciate the vibrancy of life. This was his way of recharging whenever things wore him out.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I wanted him to rest undisturbed.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Handstand walks around flowerbeds are prohibited."
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Let's not worry about how the Bloodhounds figured this one out. Hm, I reckon the worst that can happen for this one is that they'll flip you back onto your feet. Say, why don't you test it out this time? I'd love to see you do a handstand!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: No, thank you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Please do not use SoulGlad bottle caps sold by the Dreamjolt Troupe while experiencing the attractions."
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: The Dreamjolt Troupe? Where? Are they hiding or something?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Shall we give this capsule machine a try and see what happens?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Nothing's off so far. Maybe we should open the capsule?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Uh, they can't be seriously going that far, right?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Sunday unreservedly shares his story with Welt...
No, no, no! Hey, look out!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Did they have to do that!? They could've just recalled the capsule!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Perhaps making the attractions no longer just attractions is another corrective measure?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Ugh, aren't the rules being too finicky with words?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: "Do not discard trash in trashcans."
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Oh, there it is. Huh, it does look somewhat like you.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Time for it to disappear for good.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Reveal thyself unto me, as is customary — All creatures endowed with eyes bear souls of equal worth."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Whoa, it worked! The IPC totally should've sent someone to keep an eye on you. Aren't they worried that you might make a comeback in Penacony and grow a new pair of wings?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: So long as there remains a need for me to keep a low profile, I'm no threat to them.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That's true. Come to think of it, you had always been in the spotlight, be it as a respected member of the elite or a leader. When was the last time you fell into the mud? All the way back during your childhood days?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Oh, something's happening.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: What is this, a woodcutter's trashcan!?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Several weeks later, Golden Hour, Penacony
Sometime before I turned six. Like most boys would, I tried to fly with my ear feathers, only to fall into a pit. I almost broke my halo.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That was sarcasm, in case you didn't realize. But whoa, you actually remember something like that?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: You never forget times of failure. It's only human nature.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Bah, you're probably the only one who'd consider something like that a failure.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: What is it this time?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Just looking back.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But nothing's there!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: That's the whole point of revisiting a place. When I look at everything here, the memories are so fresh it's as if it all only happened yesterday.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: When the younger me tasted failure here, I ran myself ragged to fix the mess. I'd thought myself no longer the same person as before... But it looks like I was just going round in circles.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm glad for this chance to look back on my past in this way. Come now, we should go. This will be a long farewell.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So, where are we heading next?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Oti Mall. There are Bloodhounds stationed along the way, though. It might be better to take a quieter route...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I don't mean to meddle, but I'd advise you to stay away from that place.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Did something happen?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: There isn't any concrete information yet, but anomalies have been reported around the area. The Family is currently investigating.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...You okay?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'm fine.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The Stellaron incident may have been quelled, but who is to say that nobody has another agenda?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Thanks for the tip, sir. We'll make a detour. May you stay safe, too.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hold on.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Sweet dreams are technically safe, but it would be wise to look out for oncoming vehicles.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Thank you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Whew, that was no ordinary passerby. It's a miracle that he didn't see through your disguise.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: The Astral Express should've departed a long time ago. Why is he still in Penacony...?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...We needn't change our plans because of him, but be sure to keep your guard up.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I hope nothing terrible has fallen upon Penacony while I was in captivity the last few days.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Seems I let my wishful thinking get the best of me. Will you at least give me a chance to explain?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I will. But before I do...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Put your hands behind your back and answer my questions in short sentences.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Short sentences?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I need to make sure your words aren't concealing any dangerous incantations.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I can't believe I've left everyone with such a peculiar impression of me...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Please believe me when I say that I didn't come back here with ill intent. Penacony will never experience the Order again either.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm afraid I won't be taking your words at face value. Not after how you wielded the power of Harmony.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Answer me. What are you doing here?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It looks like there's only one way to gain your trust.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Come on out, Wonweek. We've found ourselves an ally.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So, it was the IPC that freed you?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: My sister has likely made an agreement of some sort with them. As for how I'm able to move around freely in Penacony, I have Wonweek to thank for that.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: As you can see, I've only returned to my home to bid it farewell. Would you be kind enough to give me a chance to say goodbye so that I may leave without regrets?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Agreed, but until you leave Penacony for good, you are to stay by my side.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You have my gratitude.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...I left my home in a hurry, too... I know how it feels.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That said, I can't make this call by myself. My companions need to know about this too.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Astral Express crew is in Penacony, too?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Come with me — we'll go find them. You come along too.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Okay, okay. Boy, this is gonna be a party!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: We're here. They should be somewhere nearby.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mr. Yang. If you don't mind, there's something that puzzles me.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Now that the crisis on the Planet of Festivities has been averted, shouldn't the Astral Express have departed to continue on its trailblazing journey? Why have you and your companions stayed behind in Penacony?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Could it be that someone stirred up trouble after I left?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And if that were indeed the case?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I doubt I'm in any position to be proposing ideas, but I'm happy to defer to the Nameless and aid with any plans you may have.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: There's no need to worry, all is well in Penacony. Our reason for lingering here is a certain unusual passenger.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: A passenger?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The Express has been commissioned to send a passenger back home. We're just resting up in Penacony for a while before we depart.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hm?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: By "passenger," do you mean this lady here?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Or...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...These ladies?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This... How...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You're finally here, Mr. Yang! We have a huge problem!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Meanwhile, {TEXTJOIN#87}
Nngh... Tsk... Phew... I'm... walking on the street...? What a weird dream...
rows.speaker: Sleepwalking Tingyun

rows.text: This Miss Tingyun looks like she's sleepwalking. Nope, not her.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yikes, she's scary! No, I won't be able to talk to her...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ooh? Heh heh heh...
rows.speaker: Money-grubber Tingyun

rows.text: She seems completely oblivious to everything else, and is just standing there, continuously operating the Cash-Spewer, occasionally letting out an excited laugh.
Why do I feel like it's not gonna be a wise move to interrupt her...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You... can't fly? Why?
rows.speaker: Kiddy Tingyun

rows.text: I can, I can fly! A long, long time ago, a big girl flew with me really high into the sky!
rows.speaker: Kiddy Tingyun

rows.text: I'll take you next time. Pinky promise?
rows.speaker: Kiddy Tingyun

rows.text: Uh... Should we get someone to watch over her?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Nah, I think she's perfectly fine on her own. The childlike innocence that adults have is a lot more resilient than you can imagine!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Even if that's true, it doesn't apply to her!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, were you all looking for me?
rows.speaker: Tingyun (?)

rows.text: "Don't question it. Keep moving forward."
It's you again. Who's talking to me?
This path is so dark, yet it's strange, the farther I walk... the more at peace I feel...
Could it be that... this isn't the first time?
That... looks so familiar.
Does she want to lead me somewhere...?
Everyone stay calm... I'll explain.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The surprises just keep pouring in... First, there was Miss Acheron, and then Miss Tingyun. Why does it seem like Mr. Yang always comes back with some extraordinary guests?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Forget about it, how are you gonna clone your bat?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey! You'd better not be referring to the part about my wits surpassing many others!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mr. Yang mentioned the Express' next voyage is to send a passenger back home. Could this lady be from the Xianzhou Alliance?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: She ought to meet your "one we can properly speak with" requirement, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It is not my intention to provoke you. Perhaps as assurance, we can have my friend here perform the task in my stead. Wonweek has a higher mastery of the Harmony than I do.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The tuning rebounded and affected Wonweek instead. This is no ordinary woman.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: A little quick to the draw, aren't you?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Bah, you don't have to tell him that! He can see for himself!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Not now, of all times!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Forget it. I'll tell you... We walked around with Miss Tingyun for a while after separating from the rest, but then we ran into something... weird.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, come on—stop interrupting. So, we had some candy and were so happy we rolled around on the ground for a bit before standing up... But once we did, we realized Miss Tingyun...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Y—You...! What's going on!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Welt fills them in on what he's been through...
I believe that at this point, Sunday has no reason to be dishonest. But to prevent any unforeseen complications, I'll be accompanying him everywhere he goes, until he leaves Penacony.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mr. Wonweek here is an old acquaintance of Sunday's.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Pleased to meet you, fair lady. And you, of course... you're the heavyweight who pummeled this control freak?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Ahem, let's leave this discussion for later. For now, we should be focusing on returning Miss Tingyun to her normal self.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That's... not gonna be easy. You'll see what I mean, Mr. Yang. These Tingyuns aren't exactly easy to communicate with.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, you're here again! So, what's your decision?
rows.speaker: Visionary Tingyun

rows.text: Uhh... I'm still deliberating. I—I'm so highly sought after that it's only right I give it careful consideration.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Aha—! I knew it, I always have an eye for talented people. No problem, take your time.
rows.speaker: Visionary Tingyun

rows.text: That sounds nice. People never forget a personally prepared home-cooked meal.
rows.speaker: Flower Enthusiast Tingyun

rows.text: But then again, gifts should be lasting. What about a delightful new bouquet of flowers on the table each day? Wouldn't they do a better job at brightening up someone's day?
rows.speaker: Flower Enthusiast Tingyun

rows.text: Hmm, that sounds like a good idea.
rows.speaker: Silver-tongued Tingyun

rows.text: If we really want to do this right though, it's the thought behind the gift that truly matters. The more thought goes into the gift, the better the recipient feels it.
rows.speaker: Foodie Tingyun

rows.text: Oh, she makes a valid point, too.
rows.speaker: Silver-tongued Tingyun

rows.text: You sure have a way of not offending anyone...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: These three Tingyun's don't look like they'll be reaching a conclusion anytime soon. We won't be able to get a word in.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So, what do you think, Sunny?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Let's try a different name, my dear friend.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Don't we sound chummier that way? I took a leaf out of this foxian girl's book.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: The problem with Miss Tingyun is just as I suspected before. That prank shattered her into notes that are each a part of her.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: In other words, it means the Tingyuns we see here are all different aspects of her psyche.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Okaaay, you just made it sound a whole lot more complicated...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: At any rate, this is a known occurrence across the Dreamscape. Tuning could be the way to fix it.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The only problem is that these Miss Tingyuns are too caught up in their own world. Is there one we can properly speak with?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: One that we can speak with...? Oh, I think there is one!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But... It may take me a while to identify her.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Tsk, looks like they still haven't decided on anything yet...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, if you ask me... Take the people pleaser out of the picture, and they'll arrive at a conclusion in no time at all.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: You're hoping for them to get into a fight, aren't you?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Found her! If I remember correctly, this Miss Tingyun's trait is...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's nothing special really.
rows.speaker: Somewhat Normal Tingyun

rows.text: Worth a try.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: My lady, if I may, I wish to perform a tuning on you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Before you start, you should know we're keeping our eyes on you. If you even think about taking Miss Tingyun hostage—
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That is true.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: If you still have concerns, you are also free to restrain me while he performs the tuning.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Um, there's no need for that. You're acting so sincere. I'm actually surprised.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are you alright with this, Miss Tingyun?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I go as the wind blows, so you may decide for me.
rows.speaker: Somewhat Normal Tingyun

rows.text: Then kindly forgive our intrusion. Please do your best, Wonweek.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The life support pod is ready. There were only minor issues.
rows.speaker: Unfamiliar Mechanic

rows.text: That's great. Otherwise, that person from the Xianzhou might not be able to hold on much longer.
rows.speaker: Unfamiliar Researcher

rows.text: You're still trying? There's no precedent for saving someone who was destroyed by a Lord Ravager. Will it even work?
rows.speaker: Unfamiliar Mechanic

rows.text: I'm not a genius, so I don't understand the logic behind it, but if she says it's possible, then it must be.
rows.speaker: Unfamiliar Researcher

rows.text: Excuse me, could you tell me where I am?
...Can they not hear me?
Feeling more awake?
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Congratulations. You attained your very first victory in this tug of war. It's a good start.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I... This is...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Let me explain.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: You were attacked by a Lord Ravager. By all rights, you should not have survived.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: But someone didn't agree with that assessment, and it just so happens I was able to fulfill his request.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: What about the other merchants?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I don't know.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Why me...?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Because you were the most unfortunate. You fell into the hands of {RUBY_B#Phantylia}that Lord Ravager{RUBY_E#} who destroyed your body and spirit.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Yet you were also the most fortunate. Her desire to claim everything about you for herself meant she needed time, so you were spared instant annihilation.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: There is only a fine line between resurrection and escaping death, yet they couldn't be more different. If you had truly died, I would have been powerless to do anything for you.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: My body... feels strange...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I'm sorry. I can't let you regain your ability to feel just yet. You'd be in excruciating pain.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Your body was contaminated by the Destruction and suffered severe damage. As I said before, these wounds will stay with you for the rest of your life.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: To prevent its resurgence, I made some minor modifications to your body — or more specifically, your tail.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: You'll have to learn to adapt to it. Unfortunately, the inescapable price of survival is often more adversity.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: ...Regardless, I'm grateful to you for saving my life.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: There's no need for that. This was merely a transaction.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: With this, the debt between the traveling merchant and me is clear.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: Who?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Don't worry about it. You should sleep for a little longer. By the time you wake up, you won't remember any of these details.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: I'll arrange for someone to send you home... which reminds me, you seem to have some dependable friends with close ties to you.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: You should go with them. It can only help with your recovery to hear more about your past.
rows.speaker: Ruan Mei

rows.text: At this point, past events revealed by the tuning recede to the darkness once more...
Are... Are you alright?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Did I pass out?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I suppose there's no point in hiding it from you anymore.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Miss Tingyun is originally from the Xianzhou. She had an unfortunate encounter with a Lord Ravager, who robbed her of her identity and left her on the verge of death. While she miraculously escaped with her life, her body suffered terrible injuries, beyond all power to heal.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: But something happened to change that outcome?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Yes, a genius got involved. She's very accomplished in the field of life sciences and managed to grant Miss Tingyun a shot at survival.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: After that, she asked the Express to escort Miss Tingyun back home. We made a stop at Penacony along the way, partly to allow her some time to convalesce.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'm so sorry. I thought no one would be affected if I hid inside a dream. I didn't expect so many mishaps to happen.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's alright, so long as nobody was hurt. Can I get something to drink? I feel like I've been asleep for ten years.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: That's fine. We should find another place to talk anyway. We drew some attention with that commotion earlier.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Shortly after—
So, is anyone going to tell me what's going on?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: March?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh, uh... About that... Why don't you ask [Trailblazer] instead! {M#He}{F#She} knows how to present things logically!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Did something happen in the Dreamscape?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Actually it's more like it was someone's fault... We met a Pepeshi filming a try-not-to-laugh challenge, and he gave us some of his candy. A type of candy that's supposed to make you fall over laughing.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, so that sort of try-not-to-laugh challenge.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I didn't really wanna do it, but {M#he}{F#she} insisted on us giving it a shot. That's how we got into this problem.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What happened?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Miss Tingyun ate the candy too, but she only sneezed non-stop! A-choo, a-choo! Sneeze after sneeze! And before we knew it, she multiplied into several Tingyuns right in front of us!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...What's your take on this?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Dreamscape is a memoria world. It is likely the candy triggered her hypersensitive mind, causing scattered memory fragments to dissociate and become entities themselves.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: There is no cause for concern. We've experienced similar incidents from time to time in the sweet dream.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Mr. Yang, who's this?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's okay, you can reveal yourself now.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I was only being careful, or we would've been stopped by the Bloodhounds more than once on our way here.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Help me remove my disguise, Wonweek.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It's been a while, everyone.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Ah...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Hee-hee...
What the...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Did any of you hear a voice just now?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: A voice?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Never mind...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Ah, look! It's working!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss Tingyun, you're finally back!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You may be small, but you're pretty amazing!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Huh? What's wrong?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oof...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: It's nothing. Just a trivial matter...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: What do you sense?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I should have let you handle it yourself. This girl is not as ordinary as she appears...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I nearly died... just now...
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Darkness descends before the eyes, reminiscent of the chaos before the birth of the universe. Amidst this chaos, a voice emerged, resonating like that of the creator...
"Don't be afraid."
What... is this place?
"No matter what you see, you only need to remember one thing."
"You're not alone."
Who... are you?
And... who am I?
Is that... where I came from?
And where does this path lead?
How can it be... Why are there still so many of them?
The ones from before weren't defeated either?
"As I said before, you can't defeat them. No one can."
"You can fall into the darkness and die alongside these scars of the Destruction."
"Or bring them with you when you return to the world here. These are your two choices."
Return to the world? What are you saying...?
Aah... No wonder those two ignored me.
Am I just a wandering spirit now?
"Close, but not quite."
So, I'm trapped between life and death, existing in a limbo?
"You can think of it that way."
...Based on what you said, even if I should wake up, these wounds that caused my death will remain on my body and never heal?
I don't understand. You appear to be trying to save me, benefactor, but why are you telling me all this?
"It's a habit of mine. I believe everyone should have the right to choose whether they wish to return to this world or not."
Be that as it may, I don't remember anything. There's nothing to help me make a choice.
"That doesn't matter. I believe the desire to live was born from nothing to begin with."
"You may also prove yourself to be the exception. I would also be pleased with that result."
...How troublesome, but I suppose that's part of living.
"Survival or Destruction is no longer a choice for you. They both now grow along the same path."
"And only by walking this path—"
"Will you break through the darkness and arrive at my side."
Where are you planning to go next?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Could you give me some time to think about it?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Shall we keep going, then?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where are we going?
What are we doing here again?
Did you forget already? Miss Tingyun is going back to the Alliance, so we're here to help her pick out souvenirs.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm not too familiar with this planet. I'm worried an unscrupulous cutthroat merchant will try to take advantage of me. Luckily, the people I want to buy these gifts for are friends you already know on the Xianzhou, so I'll be counting on both your stakeholder intuitions for recommendations!
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: As if a merchant could seriously take advantage of you...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You handed over the dream bubble gifted by Tingyun.
Welcome! How can I help you?
rows.speaker: Shop Assistant

rows.text: Hello there! It's my first time visiting the Dreamscape, so I wanted to buy some local specialties as souvenirs for my friends back home. My two friends here are more familiar with the Dreamscape and recommended your shop, so I'm here to take a look.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Why, you really know how to flatter! Go ahead — browse all you like.
rows.speaker: Shop Assistant

rows.text: First, we have Lady Fu Xuan of the Divination Commission. What do you think best suits her?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: As usual, the dream bubble smoothly presents you with a myriad of scenes—
However, you're very familiar with this dream. It's almost the same as your travels on the Luofu.
The only difference is that the foxian lady, Tingyun, who was travelling with you, never encountered the Lord Ravager. Instead, she helped you solve that crisis of her own free will.
You have a similar memory.
But you decide to keep this dream.
Next is General Jing Yuan.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Finally, we have Lady Bailu of the Alchemy Commission. She loves excitement.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Lady Fu Xuan has such refined taste? The Xianzhou really has changed a lot in the time I've been asleep.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Uhm, did you pick that because of her third eye?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Um, can you picture her driving?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's all of them. Please wrap them up for me.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's not your decision to make!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Come to Clock Studios Theme Park to learn more about the history of the Planet of Festivities!" I think the general will like this gift.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Seriously?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's a good idea. It might be commonplace, but it's still the specialty of Penacony. It would make for an ideal gift to bring home.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You carry yourself with such dignity and grace, but you still have the heart of a child. Lady Bailu loves these types of accessories. Let's go with your suggestion.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Both wings and horns? That's a little much, don't you think?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thanks to both your help, everything went smoother than I expected. And it looks like we still have some time to spare.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Why don't we pay another visit to the Dreamscape Sales Store? You can find memory bubbles pretty much anywhere, but Penacony's dream bubbles are extraordinary. Even if we don't get them as gifts, we can keep them as souvenirs for ourselves.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's just the nature of the foxians. It's widely known that mystery is the key to our allure.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But I'm not very strong physically. Are you referring to my quick wits?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That part is true. I'm always calculating when it comes to business, but never with people.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: A souvenir for myself? That's definitely an idea I can get behind.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I'll just assume that's a compliment! Maybe next time, you could just say "silver-tongued."
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Is that... a compliment? I'm not sure if I'm deserving of that title.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But there's one more thing I wish to do. Since this is our last stop, could I have a word with you two in private? Perhaps somewhere more secluded. I'd like to discuss a personal matter.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's true! I'd love to learn how you do it!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Now's not the time for those kinds of jokes...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey! No tattling!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This is a good spot.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Miss Tingyun, what's this about?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You've looked out for me during our travels together these past few days. I'm truly grateful and can't thank you enough.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: SoulGlad again... I'm a local, you know.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: You'll have to make do.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: In any case, I must thank the both of you for your assistance.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It was nothing. Now that the matter with Miss Tingyun is resolved, are we meeting your other two companions next?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: There's no need for that. Mr. Wonweek is in poor condition, so let's wrap up your farewells first.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'll leave Miss Tingyun in your hands.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Huh? But Mr. Yang, the messenger from the Xianzhou is almost here. You're not coming with us?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I trust that you can handle it. Besides, Himeko will be there. She'll be able to handle any decisions should you run into any difficulties.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Okay. We better hurry then.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But there are some things I find difficult to forget. I feel it's only right that I tell you what's on my mind before we part ways.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Do you two still remember what it was like when you first saw me?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: How could we forget? [Trailblazer] was so shocked, {M#he}{F#she} was frozen in place when {M#he}{F#she} shouted...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Exactly.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Let's go with your suggestion.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: A meticulously thought out and interesting suggestion. It'll make for a novel gift. Let's go with that.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: It looks cool, but it's probably not a good idea.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the kind of treasure I've always yearned for, but the general's position won't allow him to accept such a gift.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: And that's precisely why I haven't been able to shake off this strange feeling in the days since I started traveling with you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Now that the Alliance has all of you there to help them, sending any elite fighters more would just be overkill.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: When I asked for your names, I couldn't help but think that this "first encounter" was actually a "long-awaited reunion" for you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I've heard about what happened to you on the Xianzhou, and I've got to admit, that Phantylia's disguise was so perfect, it was like another me tricking everyone.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Yeah, we couldn't even tell when you were replaced by Phantylia.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I figured it happened when we were after Kafka. You vanished for a while, I thought you must have come back as a double.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But it was much earlier than that.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That thought has filled me with sorrow, as if a piece of my life had been stolen away, and I had no part in it.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's what I've been puzzled about too. I never actually saw how Phantylia managed to disguise herself as me.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: What was your impression of that "Tingyun," if you recall?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: So, what did she seem like to you?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Was there anything particularly memorable?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Now, the final question.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: In your eyes, am I just like the Tingyun you remember?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Wait — don't you find that question a bit weird? You're the real Tingyun. Why compare yourself to an imposter?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss March, you might have the wrong idea. I'm just feeling a mix of regret and relief.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...Huh?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: As a merchant, staying well-informed is crucial. It's only natural for me to stay updated on the events of the Luofu before I return.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If I had rushed in and out back then, I wouldn't have been much help. Instead, I would've postponed the trip and sought assistance from allies, but in that case...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: We wouldn't have crossed paths.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Exactly.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Based on your description, that Lord Ravager was indeed cunning. Her demeanor mirrored mine so closely that it felt like she was living my life for a few days rather than merely disguising herself.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I regret missing out on your Xianzhou journey, but everything that unfolded afterward, aside from the scheming, played out exactly as if I'd been there. This leads me to consider another possibility...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Phantylia had stolen a piece of my life, and a foxian always gets even. I will not be taken advantage of. I must take something back from her as well.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But after thinking it over, the only thing that could be considered equal value... is the bond I have with all of you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That thought has brought me great comfort, and now I know how to speak to you properly.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: We've never even met before, yet here you are, offering your help, just as before. I should've treated you with respect, but fear of Phantylia made me act like somebody else.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: And now, I will reclaim everything I have lost. And it should begin with a proper acknowledgment—
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Dear benefactors, I extend my heartfelt gratitude to you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Looks like we're off to a good start! Moving forward, I'll definitely be trying more things like this from now on.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: And you, my dear benefactors, will be my source of courage.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Haha, we'll see. I just hope the Tingyun in your memories won't be tainted by Phantylia anymore.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Alright. No more questions. I hope I didn't take up too much of your time. Let's continue on our way.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Welcome to the Dreamscape Sales Store! Dr. Edward at your service!
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: We're looking for some dreams to give as gifts — something exotic and, preferably, captivating.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Just a friendly reminder: Being too picky won't help you find the best dreams. It'll just dampen your spirits ahead of time.
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: Miss Tingyun, that's way too over the top. Just don't make any risky decisions. It might overwhelm {M#him}{F#her}!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That being said, there are always some lucky exceptions. Not long ago, I procured a dream bubble that sounds perfect for you.
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: The story unfolds in the Xianzhou Alliance, where a young sword master strives to become the Sword Champion. However, his junior foxian soror who's just turned a hundred, puts him in a tough spot...
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: Why does that sound oddly familiar...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Since I'm returning to the Xianzhou, I think it's better to choose something unrelated to the Alliance. Feel free to pick a few for me.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I love customers like you... So easy to work with.
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: So easy to take advantage of, you mean?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Just don't pick anything weird, okay?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, speaking of dreamscapes, I have a gift for you, my benefactors.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: After troubling you all this time, I couldn't leave without properly expressing my thanks. Here's a dream bubble for you — I hope you enjoy it.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Wow, that's really nice of you!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Here are the dream bubbles I've prepared for you. Thank you for your business!
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: Well, it looks like everything's finally in order. I suppose it's time to head back?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Oh... this is quite the dream—full of twists and turns, with all the right elements. I'd be willing to buy it back at a high price. Think about it.
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: I'll let you know after I've seen it.
Hard pass.
Then, please close your eyes—
rows.speaker: Dr. Edward

rows.text: I can't believe it's time for Miss Tingyun to leave. I'm not ready to say goodbye just yet.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You're back!
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yeah, we got delayed on the way. Mr. Yang will explain in detail when he gets back.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Has the messenger from the Xianzhou arrived yet?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yes, we've been chatting for a while. Turns out, she's an old acquaintance of yours.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Long time no see, everyone.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Madam Yukong?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I've imagined this moment many times.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: I was worried I might embarrass myself in front of you. I even rehearsed every word beforehand.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: But now it seems it was unnecessary.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Tingyun, I'm here to take you home.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: You two must have a lot to catch up on after being apart for so long. We'll give you some space.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Madam Yukong, I wasn't expecting it to be you. What a wonderful surprise!
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I wanted to come because... after all, it's you who's coming home.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Yeah, me, of all people...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Your body... It's going to be tough from now on, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: I've already escaped death once. What more could I ask for?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Also, it's not all bad. I might even beat you at arm wrestling now.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You're still the same — carefree as always.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: I have a lot I'd like to tell you, but I'll save it for the road. It's a long journey back to the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Even if we can't completely rid you of the pain, there must be ways to alleviate it on the Xianzhou.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: I have no doubt. But... since we're alone here, may I ask you one more thing?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...Do I really have to go back to the Luofu?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...Why? You don't want to?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Despite Phantylia's ruthlessness, she spared me when I should have been eliminated. And why did Miss Ruan Mei, who has no ties to the Xianzhou, go out of her way to save me?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: It seems as if I've become a pawn in someone else's game.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...There are people within the Alliance who also believe that the suspect is now on the Yuque.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: If that's the case, it's all the more reason for me not to return to the Luofu and complicate things. I might as well take advantage of this situation.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Take advantage of the situation? What do you mean?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Right now, the marks of {RUBY_B#Destruction}Ruin{RUBY_E#} inside me maintain a delicate balance. Moreover... they were created by Phantylia herself.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If possible, please inform the general and arrange for me to meet with the marshal. Maybe this body of mine can help the Alliance get one step closer to the Xianzhou's enemies.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: When Ruan Mei visited the Luofu earlier, she mentioned what happened to you. This coincided with when the message sent by the Astral Express arrived.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: The Arbiter-Generals concluded that Phantylia did not intend for you to survive. If utilized strategically, this could give the Alliance an element of surprise.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: If we follow this plan, we must keep your "resurrection" hidden. But before making any decisions, I want to know what you think. If you wish to go home...
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: I'll support you, no matter what others may say.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Then I'm glad. I shall save you the trouble of hearing what those people may say.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The road ahead is perilous. If you decide to take it, I won't stop you. Maybe I'm being selfish, but I still want to know — are you choosing this because it's what you really want?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: I've come to see myself clearly in this dream journey. Perhaps it's what people call a blessing in disguise.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: There is someone who can attest to my true intentions.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Please follow me. She should be around here somewhere.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Is that...
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: After a strange encounter, I was fragmented into multiple "Tingyuns," each embodying a different aspect of my memories.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: And one of them hasn't returned to me because she ventured too far. Until now.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...You mean her?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: What is she... doing?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: She is captivated by something that has deeply mesmerized me.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: As a fleeting emotion, she's no different from a newborn. Her boarding this ship was solely down to her inner impulse.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Madam Yukong, do you remember? Perhaps that was just an ordinary flight for you. But for a certain child...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That was her first experience with the "sky."
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Of course I remember.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Back then, you were still young enough for me to carry.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: You probably still can! Want to give it a try?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I'm afraid you'd be too heavy for me now.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Just kidding.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I remember you kept begging me to take you to the starskiff and even dreamed of becoming a pilot. But once you were airborne, you were so nervous that you clung to others for dear life.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: This flight was a turning point in my life.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The boundless cosmos unfolded before me. I was completely mesmerized, not just by the view, but by a realization—
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: In this world, there are paths beyond waiting for us to explore.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Even though I lacked the talent to pilot the starskiff and wasn't much of a warrior, I still chose to travel around with the merchant guild.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Even to this day, this thrill still courses through me.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That hasn't changed?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Never.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Now, I can embark once more on my journey as a "Traveler of No Return," exploring the paths that lie beyond.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Speaking of which, how are things with the Whistling Flames?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I've left Yanming in charge for now. He's reliable, but he can be a bit extreme, and might not always follow your principles as a traveling merchant.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: My principles...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: "Forsake what others fight for and take what others abandon. That's the way to navigate the world and achieve my goals." I will continue to uphold my principles.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But now, I've also learned that while these merchant principles may apply to humans, they falter in the face of the gods.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But this shouldn't fall on your shoulders to begin with. You are simply an innocent survivor in this war.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Madam Yukong, you were once a "survivor" in the war too, weren't you?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: In a hazy dream, I vaguely remember someone telling me that the inescapable price of survival is often more adversity, but...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Madam Yukong, the gods use humans as pawns in their cosmic game, sacrificing countless innocent souls... Have you ever thought about making THEM pay?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...Every moment of every day. But as inconsequential as we are, how can we escape the fate of being mere pawns?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: If I could choose, I would never want you to become a pawn. I just wish you could still be that carefree little fox, not caught up in this war...
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Don't be disheartened, Madam Yukong.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Thanks to the "favor" of the Lord Ravager, I've become a player in this game.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Remember, it's often the unassuming pawns — the lone traveler or the worm that subdues the dragon — that leave even the best strategists helpless.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: So now, I'll become a cunning speck of dust and make those masterminds behind the curtains...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Sneeze a few times!
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: A moment of silence lingers after that. "Departure" is often indistinguishable from "Parting," yet they are fortunate enough not to have to waver between the two.
But luck never seems to favor everyone...
Is this place also affected by the Order?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: No, I'm just here to bid farewell. I changed my mind along the way. This journey has too many variables...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So it shouldn't matter if we add another.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: How did you know she would be here?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I didn't. I had a hunch and decided to try my luck. It seems I can be lucky sometimes.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It's not like you to leave things to luck.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Meanwhile at Dream's Edge
I'm trying to change, too.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I don't think you need a bystander in this scenario. Go on ahead.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You're not worried I'll take the opportunity to escape?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I believe you're the kind of person that has the ability and desire to use everything to your advantage... but that "everything" does not include Miss Robin.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...Thank you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Now then, Mr. Wonweek...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'm not leaving. No way.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Let him stay. He won't be in the way.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I actually need Wonweek to be there. She shouldn't be seen talking to a fugitive no matter the circumstances.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You... don't intend to reveal your true identity to her?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Both parties don't have to be aware that this is a farewell.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...I shouldn't put her at risk for my selfishness.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...As you wish.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Shall we go then?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: (deep breath)...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Let's go. Our journey can't begin if I can't take this first step.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I didn't expect to see you here, Miss Robin.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It's nice to meet you, Miss. May I know your name?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: My name is... Wonweek. I'm a member of the Nightingale Family.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Oh, you're a Dreamweaver. Thank you for all your hard work. You all are the reason the Dreamscape has been able to recover from this crisis.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: You're too kind, Miss Robin. You must be very busy. What brings you here to Dream's Edge?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm taking a break. I wanted to find a quiet place to relax, ideally somewhere where I could see the stars. Before I knew it, I'd walked all the way here.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I know these stars only exist in the dream but...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Well, perhaps the dreamscape is not so different from reality.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "When we look up into the night sky, the stars aren't really there. The glimmering lights we see are merely the images of stars from long ago."
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: So, have we ever truly seen a real sky full of stars?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You're very philosophical, Miss Wonweek. You remind me of someone I know.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Do you work nearby?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: No, no. Today is my rest day. There's going to be a show later, so I came early to find a good seat.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: A show? Here?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It's somewhere farther away. They say it's a farewell performance, the kind that's better to listen to from afar than watch it performed live.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I see. In that case, the observation deck is a good choice. You can see all of Penacony from here.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Distance can make some things appear more beautiful.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Still, these stars are unfamiliar to me. I don't recognize any of them, and it makes me feel uneasy.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What makes you feel this way? Is it because the sky is so far away, or because it's the unknown?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Perhaps it's both.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The Stellaron Disaster may not have had any real consequences, but many guests still chose to check out. Now, the hotel feels quieter than before. It makes me wonder what Penacony's future will be like. I just hope it will not negatively affect you, Miss Robin.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You're too kind. I'll be fine. The disaster was unexpected, but because of it, I was able to witness many pasts and think about many futures.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: My only real regret is that I left some things unsaid.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Did the person you wanted to say them to leave?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Yes. He left in such a hurry that I didn't even get the chance to say goodbye.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Sometimes what's in your heart doesn't need to be dressed up in words. Maybe he already knows what you wanted to say.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But don't you think we should put in some effort when we want to encourage someone?
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: If you don't mind me asking, who is it that you wish to encourage?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It's someone who experienced failure recently and is about to embark on a long journey.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: There are many such people on Penacony. Failure is like the setting sun to a Dreamchaser. It's something that happens every day.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I believe they all have the willpower to start anew, especially after receiving a smile from you, Miss Robin.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But he's different. He's stronger than most ordinary people, but because of it, people have this misconception: They think that when he falls, he will stand back up faster than anyone else.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Are you saying that's not true?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It's not. Because before he stands up again, he will hesitate and agonize for ages over whether that is the right course of action.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Failure may be a good thing for someone like that. Being able to reflect on one's actions is a valuable quality to have.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Soon, I shall travel to those unfamiliar stars, none of which I recognize."
"But as long as you continue to gaze upon them from here—"
"Then those unfamiliar stars will one day be the place of our reunion."
You may be right, but I still hope that he'll never change.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Why's that?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Because I have faith in the person I remember him to be.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: He may have taken the wrong approach when he failed, but I don't think he had the wrong intentions. We once stood together at the same starting line, but now it's his turn to fly for the stars. I believe he'll find the right path, even if he has to do it alone.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: We don't have to soar into the sky together.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Because I know we'll reunite one day, up there in the clouds.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I hope so.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Miss Wonweek, may I ask a favor? There's a jigsaw here I'd like to finish before I leave.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: If I have a Dreamweaver's help, maybe I'll be able to fill in the missing pieces.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: A Dream Jigsaw? I see. I'll do my best.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Don't worry if you can't find them. Just think of it as us taking a walk together.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: I'm still inexperienced, so let's just hope we get lucky.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Thank you anyway. I expect the first jigsaw piece will be a part of the starry sky.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: As for the other piece, I hope it will symbolize wings.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: Oh, Miss Robin! I'm a big fan!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I don't get to attend every single one of your concerts, but I watch the recordings of each of them at least once. I love all of your songs! Gosh, I wish I could tell the whole world about this!
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Thank you for your support. I'll keep doing my best.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: It's done. Have a look.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You still couldn't bear to say goodbye in the end? Maybe I'm stronger than you think...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: You must try to relax on your long journey...
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: ...Brother.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: That didn't seem like a perfect goodbye.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's enough. I only meant to stay quietly by her side for a bit.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But why did you do those unnecessary things?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What things?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Those two notes. If someone finds them, they can be used as evidence against her.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Hmph, so you can do whatever you want as many times as you want, but I can't?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I don't want to live with regret for the rest of my life either.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Live with regret...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: We're almost done saying our goodbyes, right?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Yes, we only have one last stop.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But before we leave, I have a question I'd like to ask you, Mr. Yang.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'm curious. Why did you become a Nameless?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Why the sudden interest?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I always had a feeling that you would never give up on someone who needed help. After spending time with you, I'm even more convinced of this assessment.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: At this very moment, there are countless worlds above the skies still waiting for the arrival of the Astral Express, yet you and your companions have chosen to stay here. All for an "old friend" you never knew and a notorious fugitive.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: To Trailblaze means to forge ahead, yet you stop and spend precious time on people just passing by. All the while you believe this is... the natural course of action?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Miss Robin, may I stay here with you to gaze at the stars, before the show begins?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Of course! You don't have to be so courteous. I should be the one asking. This is Dream's Edge, after all, and the Dreamweavers are its true masters.
rows.speaker: Robin

rows.text: That's not what I think at all. Besides, the Watchmaker also made a similar choice.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That painting feels like a blessing, and also seems to mirror someone's resolve: Even when the broken wings no longer belong to the sky, the direction in which they fall will still be towards the stars—
And because of that, he bid farewell to the Express and never walked among the stars again in his lifetime.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Not all journeys lead to the stars." Even if we leave the Express, some Trailblazing paths will still continue.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You can think of it this way: The title of Nameless doesn't belong to any one person. Each individual will have their own view of what it means to walk this path, and will always try their best, no matter the situation.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The goal of my Trailblazing is not the unknown world, but every living being who exists under the stars.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: In my homeland, the name "Welt" means "world." It suggests that each person is a world unto themselves, and that we harbor as many possibilities as the distant stars. The connections I gain on my journey are what is most precious to me.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: This is my way of the Trailblaze and the reason why I decided to stay here.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Why me?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Like I said before, I left my home in a hurry, too. I know how you feel right now.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I also know that a person will only be able to truly face themselves once they've decided to say goodbye to their past... the same way you're doing right here, right now...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: There was never a third person with us, was there?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I told you he'd find out.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I should have known nothing could escape your keen eyes.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Since you already know Wonweek's secret, there's no need for me to build up suspense.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Let's go. We'll head straight for the finale and take our final bow in this farewell performance.
rows.speaker: Sunday
