rows.text: I know you can hide your appearance, but trespassing on restricted Family grounds is still a bold move.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Don't worry. I won't take too much time.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I was a child when I first visited the Grand Theater. I remember seeing the light behind the curtains from here and believing it to be the Morning Star guiding me toward the Land of the Dreams.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: When I returned here many years later as the head of the Oak Family, I finally learned that the light was actually a Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Now that you've returned to the stage, what are you planning to do?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Prepare for my departure. I've always believed that a person's starting point should also be his last stop.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Have you ever seen the elderly at the end of their lives? As they welcome their final moments, they invariably raise their hands, stretching their arms into the emptiness. Much like how babies also stretch their arms into the air when they are first born.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Humanity flaps their wings twice as they complete their journey: Once when they are born, and once when they die. In order to flap my own wings and soar again...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I will say goodbye here to the me of yesterday.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I really hate this face. My expressions feel so dull and lifeless.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I see. That explains why something always felt off about your appearance.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The halo above your head that symbolizes the Harmony — it's been missing since the moment we reunited.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's true that this ring was bestowed upon our people by the heavens, but that doesn't mean it can't be thrown away.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: While I was in the Gallery of Thoughts, at the entrance of the dream, I chose to completely sever the halo from myself.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Why?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I am a fugitive, after all. I must remove any chance of being detected by The Family.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Another reason is to feel pain... A pain like falling from the sky with broken wings that can keep me awake.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This is how I can cast aside all the blessings of the Harmony and the Order and, for the first time in my life, enter the sweet dream as an ordinary person.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Is that also how Mr. Wonweek came into this world?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hmph, no, you wouldn't believe the real story even if he told you.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: He was born from an accident, one that you're actually quite familiar with...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It was that try-not-to-laugh challenge. Quite embarrassing, to be honest.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I was roaming around as an ordinary person when I unfortunately fell into that Pepeshi's trap. The prank that fragmented Miss Tingyun also divided my fragile self into two.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Are you saying that he's a part of you? That's quite surprising, given that you two looked nothing alike.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You could say he's another possibility of me.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I, too, was once a child, with aspirations buried deep within. Over time, those childhood voices grew increasingly faint.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Maybe if I had made a small change in my childhood, I would have turned out to be exactly like him.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What a pity, failing to become a better version of yourself.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: So, my final farewell will be like that of Miss Tingyun: I will perform a tuning on myself and return to my complete form.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And this also means that Wonweek will vanish for good. That's why I said this was the last stop.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Is there a possibility that you will be the one who disappears?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: No, this is a foregone conclusion.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But who's to say there won't be any changes? Maybe deep down, I'm also anticipating this possibility.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Regardless of the outcome, you will have a witness.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'll be waiting for you in the audience.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Now, shall we begin?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: "Anticipating this possibility..." You've really changed. In the past, you wouldn't have tolerated any noise at all.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I'm about to embark on an unknown journey, where it will be impossible to maintain my orderly life. I will have to navigate unexpected surprises, much like today.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You're not ready at all, are you?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Much appreciated.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I feel unsettled, maybe even scared. Ever since I left Penacony, I could no longer control everything.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Don't flatter yourself. You can't control anything.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: But isn't that how it is for most people?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: My fear of the unknown may be a weakness, but your presence has shown me that surprises aren't always bad.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Meeting you has been a great help to me, and I'm glad to have discovered this side of myself. I also feel grateful for the opportunity to tell you this in person...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I truly dislike you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What? Are you sure you didn't mean the opposite?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: I must admit, many of your qualities strike a chord with me. There are times when I want to joke around, freely express my thoughts, or openly share my dislike of a person...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Or my fondness. I want to tell her that I love all her songs.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Then go for it, Sunny. You always talk about locking the bird in the cage, but you're the one who's trapped.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Look at yourself. Besides discipline and hesitation, there's nothing else in your life. If you continue living like a slab of marble, you'll break into pieces when you fall.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: But I won't become like you. I simply can't.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I dislike people who are frivolous. It makes me uncomfortable to even emulate them. If I fail, I will still uphold my principles, such as decorum and stateliness.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: As for the Harmony, my stance remains the same. Whether it's you or the Paths, if what I once doubted — or even opposed — becomes the force I must rely on in the future...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Then this time, my true heart will guide the tuning.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I'll leave it to you.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What is this? Leaving your fate entirely up to a coin flip?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: This isn't like you at all. Did you lose your mind after being run over by the Express, or were you possessed by that IPC gambler?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Failure is always the best teacher. To save more lives, you must first understand what they live for and what they die for. The best way to achieve this is through personal experience.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You see? I'm already starting to make changes.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Whether it's us merging or one of us disappearing, I'll leave the tuning to fate, and see if I can embrace all that I detest.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Only then will I truly be able to walk among the living in their world.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But what if you can't do it?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Well, that's out of my hands. It will just prove that I'm still the same person...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: The person who always disappoints his sister...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Falling is just another name for flying.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: That's why I rejoice at my broken wings.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Step into the mortal world to see how it truly is.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Then, be born as a human and die as one.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: And with my last breath, I'll join the weak... in reaching my hands toward the sky.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: On the Planet of Festivities, whatever identities I once had, they no longer matter.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: It's not the Gods who answer us, but ourselves from the future.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I don't have much to say. But as it's time to part ways, here's one last piece of advice.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: When telling jokes, be sincere. Don't sweat the details, and above all, don't explain them every time.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Ah, never mind. Maybe it's better for you not to joke at all.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: No objections from me.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: This is so annoying. How did I become so dull?
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Well, despite everything, try not to be too hard on yourself. There will always be people who are sad.
rows.speaker: Wonweek

rows.text: Mm.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Well, how should I address you now? Mr. Sunday or Mr. Wonweek?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Whichever you prefer. He's probably mocking me from inside right now.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Thank you for accompanying me through all this, Mr. Yang. This farewell journey has come to an end.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: What are your plans after leaving Penacony?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: At this point, there is no need to hide things from you. I believe there's more to the incident involving the Stellaron on Penacony.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Are you suggesting that the Dreammaster wasn't the one controlling the Stellaron?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Don't worry. The Oak Family was indeed behind seizing the Stellaron and resurrecting the fallen Aeon during the Charmony Festival, and you've already defeated them.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: But Mr. Gopher Wood once told me that all the Order's efforts were aimed at avoiding the same mistakes that the Harmony made.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: My guess is that The Family from the Montour System must be involved.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Unfortunately, too much time has passed to verify that. Penacony is just a small territory, and even the family heads with their authority cannot enter the sacred site of the Harmony and inquire about the true will of the Great One.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: In the worst-case scenario, if Xipe turned a blind eye, how could "the strong defending the weak" hold up?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Mr. Yang, I just want to tell you this: The Harmony has more than one side. THEY can be the most steadfast ally of the Astral Express or the most fearsome enemy.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Thank you for being honest with me. The efforts of the Crew on Penacony were driven by the same concern.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: After all this, the Harmony and the Preservation will keep the situation on the Planet of Festivities in balance. With the momentum from the Trailblaze, more forces will arrive, and Penacony will become a public space in the Cosmos.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Freedom is the only answer the Nameless can offer. I'm glad that Penacony needs it.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You and I both strive for a peaceful society, even if our reasons are different, and you've gone even further than I have.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: If not for our Paths, perhaps you and I wouldn't be in opposition.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Don't sell yourself short. We're not fundamentally opposed. Otherwise, you wouldn't have shown me mercy in front of the Dreammaster.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: This shared journey is my way of repaying you. After all—
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You are one of my Trailblazing goals.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: About that, you've given me many insights as well. Humans are the measure of everything, and no one is the sole savior.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Creating a paradise remains one of my lifelong ambitions. As I move forward, I realize I must build it brick by brick. Therefore, I have a request that I hope you'll consider...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: While I lack the will to Trailblaze, nor can I become a true Nameless...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: I admire your convictions. Perhaps, what I need, more than asceticism, is knowledge.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Therefore, after leaving Penacony, would you consider letting me...
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Come aboard the Astral Express and travel with you for now?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: In this battle, you were the one who directly confronted him. Your opinion holds the most weight.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But in this battle, you were the one who directly confronted him. Your opinion holds the most weight.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oh, really? But your face tells me otherwise. Come on, spill it. Your opinion holds the most weight.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I learn the most valuable lessons from my past opponents. Please say whatever's on your mind.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: You're a noble person. I can't deny that you always have compassion in your heart, even though we may view things differently.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You're a perfectionist, always trying to control everything — even when it comes to yourself. Although, we're going to be traveling further into the unknown once we leave Penacony. I guess a change of pace could do everyone some good.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You know what I'm going to say. Tons of people trusted you, but you let them all down — even your closest family. Don't you forget that.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I believe there is a way — a better way — to achieve your ideal. Seven rest days may be just a metaphor... But I look forward to the day when it comes true.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Maybe you're too pessimistic about humanity, but the Trailblaze isn't like that. We had to learn to have faith before embarking on this path. You must do the same.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Ideals are good to have, but nothing good comes from getting carried away in fantasies. I can never agree with how you dragged everyone into that world of yours just to fulfill an illusory dream.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Nothing is for certain, anyway. An enemy yesterday may be a friend today.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Anyhow, you've been an unforgettable adversary to me, even though I haven't been trailblazing for long...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: In any case, I'm gonna have to disagree with Mr. Yang...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Welcome aboard the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Come on, you're taking over as newbie.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I have nothing more to add. I'll let you all decide, then.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You should know that I'll be watching your every move.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I won't pretend I'm okay with it. You can be our passenger, but you're not joining us.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Looks like we've come to a decision.
rows.speaker: Himeko
